Seminar Title:

Synergistic Interfacial Engineering in Strontium Perovskite-MXene Nanocomposite for Advanced Room-Temperature Gas Sensing

Seminar Type:

Synopsis Seminar

Department:

Chemistry

Speaker Name:

Adyasha Das ( Rollno : 521cy3002)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Department of Chemistry, Seminar Room

Date and Time:

18 Jun 2026 11 am

Contact:

Priyabrat Dash

Abstract:

Gas sensing technology plays a pivotal role in environmental monitoring, industrial safety, and human health diagnostics, driving the urgent demand for highly sensitive, selective, and room-temperature-operable sensor materials capable of detecting toxic and hazardous gases at trace concentrations. Among the various sensing materials explored, strontium-based perovskite oxides (ABO₃), such as SrTiO₃, SrZrO₃, and SrFeO₃, have emerged as highly promising candidates owing to their exceptional chemical stability, tunable oxygen vacancy concentration, compositional flexibility through B-site substitution, and favorable surface reactivity toward a wide range of analyte gases. However, their standalone sensing performance is often constrained by limited electrical conductivity and sluggish charge transport kinetics, necessitating integration with a highly conductive functional partner. In this regard, two-dimensional Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene has garnered tremendous attention as an ideal complementary material, offering metallic conductivity, high surface area, abundant surface terminal groups (-OH, -F, -O), and tunable interlayer spacing, which together form well-defined heterointerfaces with the perovskite phase, synergistically enhancing charge transfer, analyte adsorption, and overall sensing performance. The sensing behavior of these composites can be further optimized through morphological engineering, elemental substitution, and integration of secondary functional phases such as MoS₂, enabling target-specific performance for environmentally and industrially critical gases. With this perspective, the present thesis is broadly focused on four main objectives centered on the design and development of strontium-based perovskite-Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene nanocomposites as advanced chemiresistive gas sensing platforms. The combination of strontium-based perovskite and MXene could be a potential material in enhancing the overall gas sensing property through interfacial synergy because the oxygen vacancy-rich perovskite surface would provide abundant active adsorption sites while the high conductivity of MXene would facilitate rapid charge transfer, collectively amplifying the sensor response. Keeping the eye on this, the first objective explores the usage of spherical strontium titanate SrTiO3 perovskite nanoparticles anchored over two-dimensional exfoliated titanium carbide Ti3C2Tx MXene sheets towards room-temperature chemiresistive nitrogen dioxide (NO2) gas sensing. The integration of SrTiO₃ with the 2D MXene framework establishes a well-defined heterointerface that promotes efficient charge carrier separation and enhances NO₂ adsorption kinetics. The strong interfacial coupling between the perovskite and MXene components significantly improves sensitivity and response/recovery dynamics compared to individual materials, establishing the efficacy of perovskite-MXene architectures for oxidizing gas detection (Chapter 1, ACS Applied Electronic Materials, 2024, 6, 8, 5789&ndash5804).

Literature does reveal that changing the morphology helps in enhancement of the performance, therefore tuning the morphology can be a better idea in designing efficient gas sensor. Subsequently, in the second objective, SrZrO₃-Ti₃C₂Tₓ composites with systematically varied morphologies were developed for the selective detection of methane (CH₄). Morphological tuning was found to govern the density of surface-active sites, grain boundary characteristics, and gas diffusion pathways, directly influencing sensing performance parameters including sensitivity, detection limit, and response/recovery kinetics. The study provides critical insights into how controlled synthesis conditions can be employed to optimize perovskite&ndashMXene composites for the detection of non-polar, weakly interacting analytes such as methane (Chapter 2, Manuscript Communicated).

Literature evidently suggests that designing a ternary nanocomposite further helps in the enhancement of the nanocomposite performance. Thereafter, in the third objective, Fe-substituted SrZrO₃-MoS₂-Ti₃C₂Tₓ ternary hybrid nanocomposites were developed for the selective detection of sulfur dioxide (SO₂). Iron substitution into the SrZrO₃ lattice introduces structural distortion and an elevated concentration of oxygen vacancies, while MoS₂ contributes additional heterojunction interfaces and catalytically active edge sites. The synergistic interplay among the three functional components promotes superior charge separation and gas&ndashsurface interactions, resulting in enhanced SO₂ sensing performance with improved selectivity and stability (Chapter 3, Manuscript under preparation).

To further investigate the impact of B-site engineering, the final chapter explores SrFeO₃, where complete substitution by Fe introduces abundant Fe&sup3⁺/Fe⁴⁺ redox couples, higher electrical conductivity, and improved surface oxygen exchange kinetics. Schottky-contacted SrFeO₃&ndashTi₃C₂Tₓ nanocomposite sensor was developed for trace-level acetone detection at room temperature. The SrFeO₃&ndashTi₃C₂Tₓ sensor displayed a high response of 99.5% toward 100 ppm of acetone at room temperature and was capable of detecting concentrations as low as 250 ppb, with a rapid response time of 7 s and recovery time of 23 s. The exceptional performance is attributed to the high surface area, abundant adsorbed and vacant oxygen species, defect site formation, and enlarged interlayer spacing arising from the Schottky heterointerface, which collectively facilitate favorable acetone adsorption and efficient charge transport (Chapter 4, ACS Applied Nano Materials, 2025, 8, 40, 19342&ndash19361).

The nanocomposites developed in this thesis demonstrated outstanding sensitivity, selectivity, stability, and recyclability, establishing strontium-based perovskite&ndashTi₃C₂Tₓ MXene heterostructures as highly promising platforms for next-generation environmental monitoring and industrial safety gas sensing applications.
